rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate escalates obfuscation across all seven passes while keeping risk weights conservative for this STL-heavy target. wordfreq.cpp's main functions are dominated by std::map/std::set (_Rb_tree) operations, introsort heap adjustments, and string handling — control-flow-dense, data-structure-heavy code — so FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain weights to flatten and bogus-condition the branchy main/_Rb_tree/__adjust_heap bodies, while ICALL and IGV add indirect-call and global-variable indirection to obscure the frequent libstdc++ comparator/allocator call sites; SUB and SPLIT are nearly free (arithmetic substitution and basic-block splitting) so they are enabled broadly with low cost weights to build a cheap diversity base layer, and IBR adds opaque branch redirection across the flattened regions. RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept moderate for BCF/FLA (the two most expensive transforms) because the binary is tiny (3.6 KB text) and the shootout-style hot loops in word counting are short, tolerating modest slowdown, and CorrectnessRisk is capped at 0.25 everywhere — highest for ICALL/IGV since indirecting calls and globals through STL template instantiations is the most fragile transformation — to preserve the correct end-to-end behavior already demonstrated.
